newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude paper remains firm, wet market inactive.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude paper remains firm, wet market inactive.

text.p: The North Sea crude paper market maintained the morning's firmer levels late on Friday but wet remained virtually inactive due to a traders' gathering in Norway, traders said.
A cargo of Oseberg loading around June 24 moved at dated Brent -6 cents, slightly firmer that a cargo that changed hands on Tuesday at Dated -10 cents.
The trade was the only wet market play heard.
Two July Brents moved unchanged at $17.94 and $17.,95, while two August Brents changed hands at a slightly firmer $17.94 and $17.95.
Brent intermonth spreads continued firm, with July/August assessed at -25 cents and August/September at -16 cents and September/October some six cents stronger at -12 cents.
The paper market's strength derived from the expiry of the July IPE contract, and also from Iraqi comments hinting at delays to liftings under a second 180-day period of the oil for food programme.

In New York, Iraqi Ambassador to the U.N. Nizar Hamdoon said Baghdad had no interest in delaying renewed oil sales under the recently extended "oil-for-food" accord, but would not export more oil until an effective aid distribution plan was in place.

"No, we have no interest in delaying the sales. But, we want this deal to not only be oil for money, but oil for food and medicine," said Hamdoon. "We want to be assured on food and medicine distribution."

Iraq is permitted to sell $2.14 billion worth of crude over a 180-day period, in order to buy food, medicine and supplies outlawed by broad sanctions slapped on Baghdad after its troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
CFDs maintained their five to 10 cents morning advance, with next week (June 16-20) talked at August Brent -59/54 cents, while the following week (June 23-27) was talked at -52/-47.
The next week (June 30-August 4) was talked at -43/-45 cents.
Outright levels for Brent were 28 cents higher.
IPE July Brent was at $17.72 a barrel at 1745 GMT as traders covered shorts ahead of the contract expiry.
Traders said another support for the outright value was a perception by some that the July Brent programme was smaller than expected.
The July programme released on Friday morning scheduled the equivalent of 40.5 cargoes, compared to 38.4 cargoes in June.
The heavier programme was attributed to the longer month in July and a lighter maintenance schedule.
Some traders said they were expecting an even bigger jump in volumes. But others said the loading programme was broadly in line with expectations.
Talk on the wet market was thin, despite plenty of physical Brent cargoes available, because many traders were attending a social gathering in Stavanger.
One trading house was heard bidding on Thursday at July -55 cents but most players still valued the market around the last done level of July -70 cents.
Two cargoes of Brent loading June 28-30 were kept before the five o'clock deadline, one by J Aron and the other by Koch.
